```{r}
spe <- readRDS("processed-data/00_prelim_procdat_BJM/02_QC/02b-spe_filtered_genetargonly_log-and-nonlog-norms.RDS")

labxf <- readRDS("processed-data/00_prelim_procdat_BJM/05_LabelTransfer/05-VistoXen_NMFlabelxfer_tol1e8_k100_alph0_TEST.RDS")

labxf2 <- lapply(labxf$targets,function(x){
  y <- as.data.table(cbind(rownames(colData(x)),as.character(x$nmf_preds)))
  setnames(y,c("rn","nmfpred"))
})

labxf2 <- rbindlist(labxf2)
labxf2 <- DataFrame(labxf2,row.names=labxf2$rn)[colnames(spe),]
spe$nmfpred <- labxf2$nmfpred

rm(labxf,labxf2)
gc(full=T)
```

## first smoothing
```{r}
spe$xcoord <- spatialCoords(spe)[,1]
spe$ycoord <- spatialCoords(spe)[,2]
xyspe <- as.data.table(colData(spe),keep.rownames=T)
xyspe[,isLC:=0]
xyspe[nmfpred=="LC",isLC:=1]
sum(xyspe$isLC==1) #11253

xyspe <- xyspe[,.(rn,brnum,xcoord,ycoord,isLC)]
gc(full=T)

## split back to samplewise
xyspe_list <- split(xyspe,xyspe$brnum)
rm(xyspe)
```

## step 1 knn smoothing of LC with k=20
#### note that the data.table-internalized sapply call is not the absolute fastest way to run that step (but still only takes a matter of seconds at scale here).
#### however, this approach is more transparent in that the user can take an entry of xyspe_list into the environment as v and step through the bplapply to see what's being done here, and can see that cells are always matched in the process (as opposed to working with vectors where we don't have cell ids matched up anymore. which always makes me unccomfortable, however rationally/irrationally.)
```{r}
setDTthreads(1,restore_after_fork = FALSE)
knnreslist <- mclapply(xyspe_list,mc.cores=8,FUN=function(v){
    # get nearest neighbors for each cell in the sample
    knnout <- FNN::get.knn(v[,c("xcoord","ycoord")],k = 20)
    
    # get the row indices of those k cells
    neighborslist <- apply(knnout$nn.index,MARGIN=1,FUN=list)
    # goofily, this is returns each entry as a list within a list (e.g., [[1]][[1]], [[2]][[1]], etc.). so fix that:
    neighborslist <- lapply(neighborslist,FUN=unlist)
    # make the list names the cell identifiers as a failsafe against reordering; we will use the list entry names to retrieve the neighbor indices when calculating means below
    names(neighborslist) <- v$rn
    
    # now, get the mean of LC y/n for the k nearest neighbors indexed for each cell
    # (in knnout, the first list item, nn.index, has v's row indices corresponding to those neighbors) 
    # this value is thus a probability 0-1 that, a given cell is a LC type given the LC/nonLC identity of its 20 spatial neighbors
    v[,lcpred.smooth1.k20:=
          apply(.SD, MARGIN = 1, FUN=function(x){
              mean(v[neighborslist[[x]],isLC])}
              )
      ,.SDcols = "rn"]
    return(v)
})
rm(xyspe_list)

## concatenate back into a single full-dataset table of KNN smoothing predictions based on k=20 nearest cells
xyspeout <- rbindlist(knnreslist)

## what would the domain definitions be just from these knns?
# any LC neighbor
# nrow(xyspeout[lcpred.smooth1.k20>0])
#[1] 75659

#1 lc neighbor 
# nrow(xyspeout[lcpred.smooth1.k20>0.05])
# [1] 44041


## save the resulting smoothing predictions as a table of cell ID, coords, and VMHknn smoothing step 1 prediction values
saveRDS(xyspeout,"processed-data/00_prelim_procdat_BJM/05_LabelTransfer/02-TestLCknnsmoothing_step1k20.RDS")
```
